explanation: This pole detects the 'matter at issue' frame of argumentative discourse: it fires on words that name a dispute, campaign or deliberation, or the document, meeting or stance that carries one (debate, dispute, disagreement, controversy, issue, question, protest, demonstration, rally, campaign, petition, summit, meeting, hearing, conference, talks, proposal, reform, policy, bill, amendment, vote, argument, discussion, opinion, views, essay, article, editorial, study), and on verbs of contestation or position-taking (argue, debate, discuss, oppose, question, protest, disagree, agree, contend, condemn, criticise, reject, endorse, refute, believe, address, ask, propose, support, promote). It also fires on the preposition that directly follows such a word (of, on, about, over, for, against, regarding, toward, between), even when that PP is only temporal ('the meeting on Tuesday'), but not on the same prepositions outside that frame (attributive 'the size of the room', partitive 'a cup of tea', locative 'the table on Monday', comitative or ablative with/from/by/in), and not on concrete or merely formal nouns that frame no dispute (table, dog, dinner, garden, municipality, procedure, rule, act, matter).
